claims: Identifies an Xbox 360-based Sonic Generations recompilation for Android.
Says the project uses ReXGlue; the embedded original README identifies android/ as a Gradle app and port/ as generated C++ game code.
Reports 2–4 fps and graphics issues; says USA/Europe Xbox 360 ISO is needed.
Names a Helio G99 / Mali-G57 device and reports title-screen plus Green Hill testing at about 2.5–4 fps.
Reports a Sonic skinning glitch and estimates about 370 ms/frame outside GPU presentation, attributing the main cost to guest code.
States the author may not be able to do more work on the ReXGlue version.
Sets minSdk 28 (Android 9) and arm64-v8a ABI.
ReXGlue maintainer describes ahead-of-time conversion of Xbox 360 PowerPC code to portable C++ rather than runtime interpretation/JIT.

claims: Names the exact USA v1.1 image as SCUS-94240 and requires a user-owned BIN/CUE.
Describes original R3000A gameplay execution with a native Windows host.
Calls the software a public test and lists the 20-mission campaign flow.
Describes sf_psx as implementing R3000A, GTE, bus, IRQ, DMA, CD-ROM, SPU and XA.
Assigns rendering, launcher/UI, windowing, saves and FMV to the Windows host.
Public-test release 0.2.0-beta.2 published 2026-08-13; release notes list launcher, graphics and model changes.

syphon-filter-ps1-windows-game-specific-.classification_note: Classified as Emulator because original PlayStation guest code runs in a game-specific PS1 machine runtime; no static recompilation or reconstructed matching source claim appears in the reviewed maintainer sources.

claims: Describes a native Quest 3 mixed-reality app built from the community decompilation, not an emulator.
Identifies luisxl15/Strikers-Android-Port as its Android phone port base.
Documents Quest-specific passthrough/tabletop/stadium modes, the own-game-image requirement, and says Quest 3 was tested while other headset models are untested.
Publishes QuestStrikers-alpha1.11.apk in the v0.1.11-alpha1 release on 2026-10-16.
Release notes describe online synchronization changes and Quest 2 screen adjustments; this does not override README statement that other headsets are untested.
States that the phone port shares the desktop game code/renderer, compiles the game for ARM, and is built on the community decompilation by Yannick Suter.
Describes the upstream work as a high-fidelity matching decompilation and explicitly says it is not itself a port or recompilation.

super-mario-strikers-meta-quest-3-mr-por.lineage_note: Quest README says it is a fork of the Android phone port, but GitHub API reports fork=false; describe the lineage as maintainer-identified rather than a formal GitHub fork. The new row is distinct because the app targets a Quest headset with OpenXR mixed-reality/VR modes, not a generic Android phone.
